summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder, COPD, chronic pain, and hypertension, was admitted after presenting to the ED with alcohol intoxication, hypoxia, and cough. He was agitated and disoriented on arrival, with a high blood alcohol level and signs of possible early withdrawal. He received diazepam for withdrawal symptoms, along with oral thiamine, folic acid, and multivitamins. Despite medical recommendations to continue treatment for a suspected COPD exacerbation and incomplete pneumonia therapy, James refused further interventions, including nebulizers, physical exams, and ECG. He remained alert and oriented, with stable vitals, and chose to leave against medical advice. He was discharged home with instructions to resume his medications, stop drinking, and follow up with his primary care provider for ongoing management of COPD, hypertension, pain, and abnormal blood findings.
